Senses.Note: This sense is separated from an attested literal execution request below. Different figurative readings of the same cutting formula are not multiplied into senses.

Occurrences.Kwic: 進云：為復是神通妙用，法爾如然？師云：一刀兩段。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Ying'an Tanhua (應菴曇華禪師語錄). Ying'an Tanhua answers an unnamed questioner's follow-up with the compact one-cut-two-pieces formula.

Occurrences.Kwic: 直下一刀兩段。便從脚跟下做將去。不必將心等悟。亦不須計較得在何時。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dahui Pujue (大慧普覺禪師語錄). Dahui Zonggao gives the formula as a direct imperative and immediately says to proceed from beneath one's heels without setting the mind to await awakening.

Occurrences.Kwic: 要明斯事，也須是箇一刀兩段漢始得。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Continued Essentials of Sayings from Ancient Worthies (續古尊宿語要). Fenyang Shanzhao says that one who wants to clarify this matter must be a one-cut-two-pieces person.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂。一刀兩段。未稱宗師。就下平高。固非作者。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), Changqing Huileng section. Changqing Huileng says that one cut into two pieces still does not qualify someone as a lineage teacher.

Occurrences.Kwic: 陽來日送出三門，乃問：汝介山逢尉遲時如何？師曰：一刀兩段。陽曰：彼現那叱，又作麼生？師便拽拄杖。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Strict Lineage of the Five Lamps (五燈嚴統(第10卷-第25卷)), in the explicitly headed Tangzhou Longtan Zhiyuan section (唐州龍潭智圓禪師): Longtan Zhiyuan is the exact respondent who answers Fenyang Shanzhao, ‘One cut, two pieces’; Fenyang immediately tests the answer with a further question, and Longtan pulls the staff.

Occurrences.Kwic: 生生的把個貓兒一刀兩段。可憐，可憐！好個玉面小貓兒，七條性命無事無辜斷送在南泉手裏
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (雲溪俍亭挺禪師語錄): J/J33/J33nB294.xml: exact retained passage identifies Langting Jingting as the headword utterer.

Senses.Explanation: One stroke of a blade leaves two separate pieces: the image is a single completed cut rather than repeated or partial cutting. Ying'an Tanhua and Longtan Zhiyuan make that compact result a short public answer; Dahui Zonggao makes it a direct command in daily activity; Fenyang Shanzhao calls for a 'one-cut-two-pieces person'; and Changqing Huileng checks the formula by saying that even one cut into two pieces does not yet qualify someone as a lineage teacher. These named answer, command, person-label, and critical uses establish a reusable formula and the Chan bend while leaving the figurative object unspecified.

Senses.PreferredTarget: to cut a person in two with one stroke
SearchAliases: split in two with a blade
Senses.Note: Xingkong Miaopu's defining allowlisted narrative is curated for this literal sense. Other apparent concrete uses must be checked passage by passage rather than inferred from the phrase alone.

Occurrences.Kwic: 如今正好乘時，便請一刀兩段。乃大呼：斬！斬！
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Complete Book of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), Xingkong Miaopu section. Facing bandits, Xingkong Miaopu asks to be cut in two with one stroke and then cries for them to cut.

Senses.Explanation: The same words can request an actual execution: one blade stroke cutting a human body into two pieces. Facing bandits, Xingkong Miaopu says that the time is right, asks them to cut him in two with one stroke, and cries for them to cut. This bodily event is a different thing from the stock answer and appraisal formula, so it remains a separate provisional sense.
